title: The Ocean at the End of the Lane
author: Neil Gaiman
description: A delicate, haunting fable about memory, childhood, and the ancient magic hidden in the quiet corners of the countryside.
quote: I liked books. Books were safer than other people anyway.

title: Legends & Lattes
author: Travis Baldree
description: An exhausted female orc barbarian decides to hang up her sword and open the first-ever coffee shop in a fantasy city.
quote: Things don't have to stay the way they've always been.

title: A Psalm for the Wild-Built
author: Becky Chambers
description: Centuries after robots gained self-awareness and wandered into the wilderness, a tea monk meets a robot asking: 'What do humans need?'
quote: You don't need to have a purpose. You're allowed to just be.

title: The House in the Cerulean Sea
author: TJ Klune
description: A by-the-book caseworker is sent to inspect a remote orphanage on an island inhabited by six magical children and their eccentric caretaker.
quote: Don't you wish you were here?

title: Before the Coffee Gets Cold
author: Toshikazu Kawaguchi
description: In a small back-alley cafe in Tokyo, customers are offered the chance to travel back in time, provided they return before their coffee cools.
quote: Water flows from high places to low places. That is the nature of gravity.

title: Kiki's Delivery Service
author: Eiko Kadono
description: A young witch leaves home on her thirteenth birthday with her talking black cat to spend a year living on her own in a seaside town.
quote: We each need to find our own inspiration.

title: The Goblin Emperor
author: Katherine Addison
description: The half-goblin youngest son of the Emperor unexpectedly inherits the throne after a tragic airship explosion, navigating court intrigue with empathy.
quote: It is a heavy thing, to be king.

title: The Little Prince
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
description: A stranded aviator in the Sahara meets a young prince who has fallen to Earth from a tiny asteroid, sharing gentle wisdom on love, loss, and seeing with the heart.
quote: It is only with the heart that one can see rightly; what is essential is invisible to the eye.
